finding: The repository publishes four HTML trees and two tool suites at once: this audited dashboard at the root (legacy Pages build from main /), session arena-01b698ef's register dashboard under review/, and two builds of session arena-009ec582's site under archive/session-009ec582/ and docs/. finding: GitHub Pages API reports legacy publication from main at /, while .github/workflows/pages.yml also deploys an Actions artifact built from docs/. finding: The published Week 10 snapshot claims 28 clubs and omits three clubs that the official hub does populate. Of the 28 clubs playing Week 10, data/injuries_2026_wk10.csv holds 24. The builder now derives the expected club set from the fixture list, and count claims are metrics rather than prose.

finding: data/depth_charts.json leaves the Kansas City left-tackle starter unasserted (a name collision was refused rather than guessed), so the first name in that group is the 2nd-string Diego Pounds. finding: The published GitHub Pages site was serving the wrong tree. Two deploy mechanisms ran on every push to main: .github/workflows/pages.yml uploaded the docs/ directory, while the repository Pages configuration builds the root as a legacy source. docs/ is an older 16-page archived build; the canonical audited dashboard is 22 pages at the root. The Actions artifact won the race, so the archive was live and every canonical page returned 404.
evidence: Probed live 2026-11-12: GET /defense.html returned 200 with the title "Defense — NFL2" (a page that exists only in docs/); GET / returned 200 with the docs/ title "NFL Intelligence Dashboard" while the root build titles itself "NFL2 — Decision Dashboard"; GET /line-origination.html and GET /depth-impact.html both returned the GitHub 404 page "404 - Flag on the Play" although both files are committed at the root. Directory listings confirm the sets are disjoint: docs/ has 16 pages, 8 of which exist nowhere else; the root has 22, 14 of which exist nowhere in docs/.
decision_impact: Was blocking for delivery (R-27, R-28, R-40): the audited site the owner was told to read was not the site that was live. Fixed by pointing the workflow at the repository root; docs/ is retained and stays reachable at /NFL2/docs/. tools/verify.py now fails if pages.yml ever targets docs/ again. Also note this falsified an earlier confirmation claim in this session, which is corrected in the board.

finding: The Week 10 injury register is a timestamp, not a state. No row was withdrawn and no player URL key changed, so the earlier transcription was correct at its own timestamp.

finding: The vendored community archive writes ARI where the league writes AZ, and LA where the league standings write LAR. A join between the two on team code, with no alias table, silently drops all nine Arizona Cardinals games from weeks 1-9 and mis-keys every Rams game. The model still reports an error rate, which is what makes this dangerous rather than merely wrong.

finding: The canonical register asserted "no price data of any kind" (FL-10). finding: The archive column this project would benchmark against is undocumented in the one place that defines it: the upstream schema file was last edited 2020-05-13, defines spread_line and total_line without a vintage (open or close), and does not mention the moneyline or spread-odds columns at all. A file named closing_lines.csv stops at the 2018 season.

finding: The injury hub renders each fixture with the national rightsholder only (NBC for the Sunday-night game, ESPN/ABC/ESPN2 for Monday), while the published schedule column carries the full list including the streaming and simulcast rights. A reader diffing the two strings sees a mismatch where there is none.

finding: Two computed results contradict conventional assumptions and neither has been resolved: home-field advantage measured on the 2026 log is 0.50 points with a 95% interval of -1.80 to +2.80 (so the customary 2.5 is outside it), and the model's own totals are worse than a do-nothing league mean (11.165 vs 11.078 points of absolute error).
evidence: data/measured_correlations_a392.csv row M-06 and data/model_verdict_2026_a392.csv total rows
decision_impact: Do not publish our total as a line; publish it as a diagnostic. Do not hard-code a home field in any model without labeling it a prior. Both are one-season measurements, so neither should be "corrected" by fitting more of the same season.

finding: Table filters on the site were being ignored silently. The csv directive parser only accepts a filter clause written as key=value, and dropped any other form without a word, so three published tables had no filter at all: injuries.html 'the six designations that were published' listed all 254 rows instead of the 6 designated ones (and its directive had also lost its closing braces, so for a time the page printed raw template text instead of a table), and suggestions.html Tier 1 and Tier 2 both listed the same 36 rows - the page the owner reads to choose a path showed the same list twice under opposite headings.
evidence: content/injuries.md and content/suggestions.md directives; tools/build_site.py render_csv_table, line 'filters = [f for f in ... if = in f]'; row counts measured by re-rendering each directive in isolation
decision_impact: The unfiltered sections read as if the site had lost the designations and as if every suggestion were tier 1. A silent no-op is the worst failure a filter can have, because the table still renders and the caption still claims a subset.
status: fixed in this build: the parser now raises BuildError for a filter clause that is not key=value or names a missing column; the three directives are repaired (new ':*' style non-blank operator 'field=*', and suggestions tiers filtered on decision); check_site now fails on any stray open brace and verify.py asserts the designation count against the file

finding: Same defect, found from the other side: the deploy mechanism did not match the served tree. This session noticed that pages.yml uploaded docs while the Pages API reported legacy publication from main at /, and that a failed Pages run (PR #30 head 7963d2b7, 22:40Z) changed nothing a reader could see. Session 8361cc7a found the same thing by fetching the site and proved it the only way that counts - GET /defense.html returned 200 while GET /line-origination.html returned 404 - recorded as FL-26 and fixed in PR #34, which repointed the artifact at the repository root behind a pre-flight check. What is left is mine to record: the two mechanisms still both run, and no session in this sandbox has ever seen its own site, because egress excludes github.io.
evidence: gh api repos/kanlerxz87-cyber/NFL2/pages -> build_type legacy, source main, path /; gh api pages/builds -> 'built' for 9af81a7f at 22:52:40Z and for 57e6888c at 22:58:23Z; gh run list --workflow pages.yml -> success on 01aeb04c, 40075341, 2386c510 and 9af81a7f, then FAILURE on 57e6888c at 22:58:01Z; gh run view 43324685409 --json jobs -> every step succeeded including actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3, only 'Run actions/deploy-pages@v4' failed; the job annotation reads 'Error: No artifacts named "github-pages" were found for this workflow run' with the action's own advice 'Fetching artifact metadata failed. Is githubstatus.com reporting issues with API requests, Pages, or Actions? Please re-run the deployment at a later time.'; gh run rerun and gh workflow run pages.yml both refused from this sandbox with HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'; then: gh run list for 4b897e55 -> 'GitHub Pages: completed/success' and 'pages-build-deployment: completed/success', gh api pages/builds -> built at 23:05:48Z
decision_impact: Two mechanisms deploy the same site and only one of them is load-bearing. While Pages is in legacy mode the red Actions run is noise, but it is noise with teeth: a session that treats 'the Pages workflow is green' as the deployment proof will now sometimes see red on a commit that published fine, and a session that treats a green run as proof will be wrong in the other direction, because the bytes are served by the legacy build. Also unfixable from a sandbox: no agent session here can re-run a failed workflow or dispatch one, so a genuinely stuck deploy has to be retried by a push or by you. Practical rule for the next session, now recorded: one red GitHub Pages run is not evidence of an outage - read the Pages API build record for the same commit before believing either. And no agent here can re-run a failed workflow (403), so 'retry later' is the only available remedy.
status: RESOLVED AS TRANSIENT, on the evidence this branch asked for. PR #38 merged to main at 4b897e55 and that commit's run of the same workflow passed every step, including the 'Run actions/deploy-pages@v4' step that failed on 57e6888, while the legacy pages-build-deployment also reported built at 23:05:48Z. So: one intermittent artifact-metadata fetch inside deploy-pages, self-clearing on the next push, exactly as the action's own error message advised. The design question in FL-23 (two deploy mechanisms, which one is canonical) is still open and belongs to the deployment owner; this row is closed.

finding: The published standings table was one game stale when this session opened the repository. nfl.com made the Week 10 Thursday-night game official (WAS 24, NYG 21) after the last build, and data/standings_2026.csv still carried NYG at 5-2-1 with 182 points for and 172 against, and WAS at 2-5-1 with 172 for and 202 against. Both rows are refreshed in this session. The defect is not the two numbers: it is that nothing on the site records when a season-to-date table was last read, so this kind of staleness is invisible until somebody re-fetches and compares.
evidence: Live nfl.com/standings read at 2026-11-13T06:50Z returns NYG 5-3-1 / 203 / 196 and WAS 3-5-1 / 196 / 223; the repository file held 5-2-1 / 182 / 172 and 2-5-1 / 172 / 202. The two deltas are +21 for and +24 against for NYG and +24 for and +21 against for WAS, which is exactly one 24-21 game. League totals moved from 6246-6246 to 6291-6291 and club-games from 272 to 274, so exactly one game had settled and nothing else. nfl.com/scores/2026/week-10 confirms only that one game is Final.
decision_impact: Every derived number that reads the standings inherits the error - the ratings, the luck residuals and the fair-line baseline all do - and no reader can see the capture time. The two rows are fixed here; the general case needs a cadence decision.
status: corrected in this session for the two rows; the missing capture-time discipline is open (Q-40, S-43)

finding: The Week 11 schedule transcription in this repository disagrees with nfl.com on the broadcaster of two games. The repository has MIA at BUF on FOX and TB at DET on CBS; the official schedule page now shows MIA at BUF on CBS and TB at DET on FOX. The swap is exact - only these two games, both in the 1:00 PM window. Either the league moved them between 12 and 13 November, or the earlier transcription swapped them. Not edited here, because this repository publishes a disagreement with an official page as a flag rather than quietly correcting it.
evidence: nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-11 read at 2026-11-13T06:52Z: "Dolphins at Bills, Sunday, November 22nd, 1:00 PM, CBS" and "Buccaneers at Lions, Sunday, November 22nd, 1:00 PM, FOX". data/schedule_week11_2026.json publishes the same two fixtures with FOX and CBS respectively. All 13 kickoff days and times, both flexed games (JAX at NYG 4:25pm, PIT at PHI 1:00pm) and the six-club bye list agree.
decision_impact: Low - a broadcaster is not a model input. But it is a live disagreement between this site and the league page, and whether to edit two cells or record that the league moved them is a decision a session cannot make on its own, because it cannot tell the two explanations apart.

finding: The site now publishes two different answers to the same question - how much of the Week 10 slate the injury record covers. The Dashboard tile and the injuries page read '{{metric injury_coverage}}' (24 of 28 clubs) from data/injuries_2026_wk10.csv, which is the 2026-11-12 capture. The Availability Watch page publishes 28 of 28 from the 2026-11-13T12:45Z transcription, because the official hub now carries full blocks for SEA and CIN and answers for LAC and BAL. Both numbers are sourced and both are true of their own moment; a reader who lands on two pages cannot tell which one is current. This session did not edit the older register - it belongs to another session's dataset - so the disagreement is published instead of silently resolved.
evidence: Official hub read 2026-11-13T12:45Z: SEA block lists 15 players, CIN block lists 8, LAC and BAL read "No Injuries Reported". The 2026-11-12T22:35Z read held SEA at 15 and CIN at 4 but the 2026-11-12T04:45Z capture behind data/injuries_2026_wk10.csv holds neither club. Club count in that file: 24 of the 28 clubs on the slate.
decision_impact: Material for any availability feature: a model reading the older register treats four clubs as unknown when the league has published all four. Resolving it is a re-transcription decision (Q-42), not a code change, and it must not be done by editing another session's file.
status: open - published, not edited; Q-42 decides the canonical register

finding: The injury hub is volatile enough that a single snapshot cannot distinguish a genuine change of condition from a filing refresh. Between two reads 14 hours apart, 17 players were added, none were removed, and 49 of the 277 players present in both reads changed practice code - 37 toward full participation, 12 away from it - while not one newly listed player carried an injury description. A model that scores the level rather than the delta will price a Wednesday filing as news.
evidence: Compared player by player: data/injuries_wk10_2026_hubrefresh.csv (2026-11-12T22:35Z, 279 rows) against data/availability_watch_c3ec1487.csv (2026-11-13T12:45Z, 296 rows). 49 practice-code changes, 17 additions, 0 removals, 0 new injury cells. Two named cases: Tony Pollard (TEN) full to did-not-practice, the largest downgrade; Kerby Joseph (DET) limited to full and OUT anyway.
decision_impact: Blocking for the surprise signal (S-12) and for gate AW-2: the read cadence has to be a decision (Q-43) before the delta can be treated as information rather than noise.
